source_text:
Non omittam ipsius etiam conversationis haereticae descriptionem, quam futilis, quam terrena, quam humana sit, sine gravitate, sine auctoritate, sine disciplina, ut fidei suae congruens. Inprimis quis catechumenus, quis fidelis, incertum est; pariter adeunt, pariter audiunt, pariter orant, etiam ethnici, si supervenerint; sanctum canibus et porcis margaritas, licet non veras, iactabunt. Simplicitatem volunt esse prostrationem disciplinae, cuius penes nos curam lenocinium vocant. Pacem quoque passim cum omnibus miscent. Nihil enim interest illis, licet diversa tractantibus, dum ad unius veritatis expugnationem conspirent. Omnes tument, omnes scientiam pollicentur. Ante sunt perfecti catechumeni quam edocti. Ipsae mulieres haereticae, quam procaces! quae audeant docere, contendere, exorcismos agere, curationes repromittere, forsitan et tingere. Ordinationes eorum temerariae, leves, inconstantes. Nunc neophytos conlocant, nunc saeculo obstrictos, nunc apostatas nostros, ut gloria eos obligent, quia veritate non possunt. Nusquam facilius proficitur quam in castris rebellium, ubi ipsum esse illic promereri est. Itaque alius hodie episcopus, cras alius; hodie diaconus qui cras lector, hodie presbyter qui cras laicus. Nam et laicis sacerdotalia munera iniungunt.
De verbi autem administratione quid dicam, cum hoc sit negotium illis, non ethnicos convertendi, sed nostros evertendi? Hanc magis gloriam captant, si stantibus ruinam, non si iacentibus elevationem operentur. Quoniam et ipsum opus eorum non de sue proprio aedificio venit, sed de veritatis destructione, nostra suffodiunt, ut sua aedificent. Adime illis legem Moysi et prophetas et creatorem deum, accusationem eloqui non habent. Ita fit, ut ruinas facilius operentur stantium aedificiorum quam exstructiones iacentium ruinarum. Ad haec solummodo opera humiles et blandi et summissi agunt. Ceterum nec suis praesidibus reverentiam noverunt. Et hoc est, quod schismata apud haereticos fere non sunt, quia cum sint, non parent. Schisma est enim unitas ipsa. Mentior, si non etiam a regulis suis variant inter se, dum unusquisque proinde suo arbitrio modulatur quae accepit, quemadmodum de suo arbitrio ea composuit ille qui tradidit. Agnoscit naturam suam et originis suae morem profectus rei. Idem licuit Valentinianis quod Valentino, idem Marcionitis quod Marcioni, de arbitrio suo fidem innovare. Denique penitus inspectae haereses omnes in multis cum auctoribus suis dissentientes deprehenduntur. Plerique nec ecclesias habent; sine matre, sine sede, orbi fide, extorres, sua in vilitate vagantur.
thought_title: The shameless disorder of heretical life
orientation: Tertullian has just argued that heresy is a kind of idolatry, and now he describes the conduct of heretics themselves to show that their way of life matches their false faith.
pass_a_gloss: I will not omit also a description of the heretical way of life itself, how worthless, how earthly, how merely human it is, without seriousness, without authority, without discipline, as befitting its faith. First of all, who is a catechumen, who is a believer, is uncertain; they approach equally, they listen equally, they pray equally, even pagans, if they happen to come in; they will throw the holy thing to dogs and pearls to pigs, although not true ones. They want simplicity to be the overthrow of discipline, whose care among us they call pandering. They also mix peace indiscriminately with everyone. For it makes no difference to them, although they handle different things, as long as they conspire for the overthrow of the one truth. All are puffed up, all promise knowledge. They are perfect catechumens before they are taught. The heretical women themselves, how shameless! who dare to teach, to dispute, to perform exorcisms, to promise healings, perhaps even to baptize. Their ordinations are rash, fickle, unstable. Now they appoint novices, now those bound to the world, now our apostates, so that they may bind them by glory, because they cannot by truth. Nowhere does one advance more easily than in the camp of rebels, where merely being there is to deserve it. And so one is bishop today, another tomorrow; today a deacon who tomorrow is a reader, today a presbyter who tomorrow is a layman. For they also impose priestly duties on laymen. But what shall I say about the administration of the word, when this is their business, not converting pagans, but overturning our people? They seek this glory more, if they bring about ruin for those standing, not if they bring about raising for those lying down. Since their work too does not come from their own building, but from the destruction of truth, they undermine our things, so that they may build their own. Take away from them the law of Moses and the prophets and the creator God, they have no accusation to speak. So it happens that they more easily bring about the ruins of standing buildings than the constructions of lying ruins. For these works alone they act humble and flattering and submissive. But otherwise they do not know reverence even for their own leaders. And this is why schisms are almost nonexistent among heretics, because although they exist, they do not obey. For schism is unity itself. I lie, if they do not also vary among themselves from their own rules, while each one arranges what he received according to his own judgment, just as the one who handed it down composed those things from his own judgment. The progress of the matter recognizes its own nature and the custom of its origin. The same was permitted to the Valentinians as to Valentinus, the same to the Marcionites as to Marcion, to innovate faith from their own judgment. Finally, all heresies, thoroughly examined, are found disagreeing with their own authors in many things. Most do not even have churches; without mother, without seat, bereft of faith, exiled, they wander in their own worthlessness.

choices.why: Conversatio here means conduct or manner of living, not conversation in the modern sense; 'way of life' captures the behavioral focus of the passage.

choices.english: the holy thing to dogs and pearls to pigs
choices.why: This echoes Matthew 7:6; 'the holy thing' preserves the neuter singular sanctum, and 'pigs' is more literal than 'swine' for porcis.
rejected: what is holy to dogs and pearls to swine
the holy to dogs and pearls to hogs

choices.why: Prostratio means a throwing down or overthrow; 'overthrow' conveys the destructive intent against church discipline.
Lenocinium means pimping or pandering; 'pandering' preserves the moral accusation that heretics treat church discipline as a form of prostitution.
Castra is a military camp; 'camp of rebels' keeps the military metaphor Tertullian uses for heretics as insurgents against the church.

choices.english: they wander in their own worthlessness
choices.why: Vilitas means cheapness or worthlessness; 'worthlessness' captures the contempt Tertullian expresses for heretics without a church home.
rejected: they wander in their own baseness
they roam in their own cheapness

pass_b_english: I will not pass over a description of the heretical way of life itself: how worthless it is, how earthly, how merely human, without seriousness, without authority, without discipline, as befits their faith. First of all, no one can tell who is a catechumen and who is a believer. They enter together, listen together, pray together, even pagans, if they happen to come in. They will throw the holy thing to dogs and pearls to pigs (Matthew 7:6), though the pearls are not genuine. They want simplicity to mean the overthrow of discipline, and they call our concern for discipline pandering. They also mix peace indiscriminately with everyone. It makes no difference to them, even though they hold different doctrines, as long as they conspire together to attack the one truth. They are all puffed up; they all promise knowledge. Their catechumens are complete before they are taught. And the heretical women, how shameless they are! They dare to teach, to argue, to perform exorcisms, to promise healings, perhaps even to baptize. Their ordinations are reckless, fickle, unstable. One day they appoint novices, the next day men bound to the world, the next day our apostates, so that they can bind them by honor since they cannot by truth. Nowhere is advancement easier than in the camp of rebels, where merely being there is a merit. So one man is bishop today and another tomorrow; today a deacon who tomorrow is a reader; today a presbyter who tomorrow is a layman. For they impose priestly duties even on laymen.

And what shall I say about their handling of the word, when their business is not converting pagans but overturning our own people? They seek this glory more: to bring ruin on those who stand, not to raise up those who lie fallen. Since their work does not come from building their own structure but from destroying the truth, they dig under ours to build their own. Take away from them the law of Moses, the prophets, and God the Creator, and they have no accusation left to speak. So it happens that they more easily reduce standing buildings to ruins than raise up what has fallen. Only for this work do they act humble, flattering, and submissive. Otherwise they show no reverence even for their own leaders. And this is why there are almost no schisms among heretics: because when schisms exist, they do not obey. For their very unity is a schism. I am lying if they do not also vary from their own rules among themselves, since each one arranges what he has received according to his own judgment, just as the one who handed it down composed it according to his own judgment. The development of the thing reveals its nature and the custom of its origin. The Valentinians were allowed the same thing as Valentinus, the Marcionites the same as Marcion: to innovate the faith according to their own judgment. In fact, when all heresies are thoroughly examined, they are found in many points disagreeing with their own founders. Most of them do not even have churches: without a mother, without a seat, destitute of faith, banished, they wander in their own worthlessness.

problems.why: 'orbi fide' = 'destitute/orphaned of faith'; 'extorres' = 'banished/exiles'. 'Exiled from the faith' conflates both; 'orbi' means destitute/orphaned, not exiled.
problems.ruling: Latin 'orbi fide' means 'bereft/orphaned of faith', not 'exiled from the faith'; translation changes the meaning.

fixed: Changed 'exiled from the faith, banished' to 'destitute of faith, banished': source 'orbi fide, extorres' — 'orbi' means destitute/orphaned, not exiled; 'extorres' means banished.

problems.quote: they more easily produce the ruins of standing buildings than the construction of fallen ruins.
problems.fix: Read as 'than the building up of what has fallen.'

edits.old: they more easily produce the ruins of standing buildings than the construction of fallen ruins.
edits.new: they more easily produce the ruins of standing buildings than the building up of what has fallen.

fixed: Changed 'the construction of fallen ruins' to 'the building up of what has fallen' to avoid the self-contradiction while matching the source's contrast between 'ruinas' (ruins) and 'exstructiones' (constructions/building up).

last_rejected.quote: They want simplicity to mean the overthrow of discipline
last_rejected.why: 'Prostrationem' means prostration/leveling, not 'overthrow'; the sense is reducing discipline to the ground.
last_rejected.fix: They want simplicity to be the prostration of discipline
last_rejected.ruling: ‘prostrationem disciplinae’ = laying discipline low; “overthrow of discipline” conveys same meaning.

last_rejected.quote: For their very unity is a schism.
last_rejected.why: The Latin says 'unity is itself a schism'—their unity constitutes schism. The English reverses the emphasis, making schism the subject.
last_rejected.fix: For unity itself is a schism.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin: schism is unity; English: unity is a schism – equivalent meaning, no substantive change.

polish.changed: Clarified the contradictory phrase about ruins and building, made the contrast between reducing standing buildings to ruins and raising up what has fallen natural and readable, and smoothed sentence rhythm throughout while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.
